organization.name: The Divided Saint
organization.entry:
The Divided Saint is a heretical cult devoted to recovering what its members believe are the scattered remains of Saint Orra.

They are wrong.

Public Knowledge

The cult operates in Fogport’s streets, piers, tram stations, and old industrial districts. Its members wear related pointed hoods made from patched oilcloth, leather, and tarnished brass. They carry relic boxes, wheeled shrines, storm lanterns, cages of moths, and large brass bullhorns.

They claim to serve a hidden aspect of Saint Orra, Fogport’s oldest saint. The legitimate Church of Saint Orra rejects them completely.

Saint Orra

Saint Orra predates House Heliot and lived roughly three centuries ago, when Fogport was still the small island settlement of Fogfort.

During the Black Founding Storm, 372 years ago, the lighthouse chapel’s beacon went dark. Saint Orra climbed the chapel tower and burned its pews, books, doors, and roof to keep one harbor light alive for three nights. More than a hundred boats followed that light home.

At dawn, Saint Orra was gone. Scorched footprints went up the tower, but none came down.

The storm brought Fogport’s first green fog. It never left. Fogfort was thereafter renamed Fogport, and the storm is considered the city’s official founding.

Saint Orra is the patron of sailors, lamplighters, tram conductors, missing children, and anyone trying to find the way home. Her great statue stands at St. Orra’s Colossus, the district named for the statue itself.

Fogporters insist: Orra belongs to the city.

The Cult’s Beliefs

The Divided Saint calls Orra the Storm Caller, the Black Lantern, and the Woman Beneath the Weather. Its street sermons claim that Orra was divided during the founding storm, scattering her body, voice, memory, and power throughout Fogport.

The cult claims that fragments of the Saint survive in old bones, severed hands, damaged lamps, buried objects, drowned corpses, and people lost in the fog. Its mission is to find those fragments and restore Saint Orra.

The Street Masses

The cult holds public street masses in rain, fog, and tram smoke. A brass bullhorn sounds down an alley, followed by the question: “Who called you home?”

The crowd is asked to name someone missing, dead, drowned, forgotten, or far away. Cultists ring handbells, release moths, burn damp scraps of paper, and pour black water into the gutters. Sometimes they invite the crowd to follow a crawling relic through the streets.

Desperate parents, sailors, lamplighters, and families of drowned workers sometimes attend, hoping for answers. The cult is especially popular among people who believe Saint Orra’s legitimate church has become too respectable.

The Relics

The most famous relic is the Reaching Hand, a pale arm kept inside a small wheeled shrine. The cult claims it once belonged to Saint Orra. The hand occasionally moves on its own, reaching toward stormwater, old stone, harbor bells, lamps, and people who have survived drowning.

Other relics include brass vessels said to contain thunder, moths that gather around hidden objects, scorched bones, lamps that burn with cold dark flames, teeth that whisper names, pieces of the first lighthouse chapel, and cages containing things that should not still be alive.

Public Rumors

  • The cult is trying to resurrect Saint Orra. Likely.
  • The Reaching Hand belonged to Saint Orra. Possible, but unproven.
  • The cult can find missing people. Sometimes true.
  • The cult kidnaps children. Partly true; several missing children were last seen near its masses.
  • The moths carry pieces of Saint Orra. Probably false.
  • The bullhorns can call storms. Possible; storms have followed several large masses.
  • The cult caused recent tram accidents. Uncertain, but plausible.
  • The legitimate Church wants the cult destroyed. True.
  • The Civic Order secretly protects them. Unproven.
  • The cult has found something beneath St. Orra’s Colossus. Very likely.

gm_post.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The Divided Saint
gm_post.entry:
The Truth About Saint Orra

Saint Orra was exactly what her religion claims: a brave and compassionate woman who sacrificed the lighthouse chapel to guide ships home. She was not an eldritch storm-being, and she did not call the Black Founding Storm.

The cult has mistaken a genuine miracle of courage for evidence of a hidden supernatural identity. But its mistake has brought it into contact with something real.

The Unreturned

The Reaching Hand is not Saint Orra’s. It belongs to an ancient revenant-like being buried beneath the oldest foundations of Fogfort. Its true name is lost. The cult calls it the Storm Caller, the Black Lantern, the Weatherless King, the Saint Beneath the Water, and the One Who Was Not Buried.

It may once have been a human sorcerer, ruler, or prophet. It is now closer to a lich, drowned revenant, or storm-bound corpse than a living person. Its body was divided and hidden beneath the island. The Black Founding Storm may have imprisoned it—or been its failed attempt to escape.

The permanent green fog is not necessarily caused by the Unreturned. But the Unreturned knows the fog, and it has begun answering the cult.

The Reaching Hand

The hand is one fragment of the Unreturned. It reaches toward the entity’s other remains and reacts to people exposed to its influence: drowned survivors, the lost, wild magic, old chapel stones, Lumen machinery, and children who dream of dark water.

The cult interprets the hand’s movements as Saint Orra’s guidance. In reality, it is guiding them toward its master.

Byl and Lott

The cult sees Byl’s wild magic as a storm symptom: reality separating, vanishing, and returning incorrectly. It may call him the White Spark, the Unlit Lantern, or the Boy Who Makes Silence. It may try to recruit or abduct him to test whether the Reaching Hand recognizes him.

The cult sees Lott as an ideal Bearer: powerful, difficult to kill, and capable of carrying a relic shrine through dangerous streets. It may offer him an honored place among them. The hand may reach toward him because the Unreturned wants a body capable of carrying more than one relic.

The cult’s most dangerous plan is to use Byl as a magical key and Lott as a physical vessel. They do not understand what they are doing.

Story Opportunities

  • A bullhorn mass begins using Byl’s name before the cult has met him.
  • The Reaching Hand reaches toward Lott in front of the Twisted Eel.
  • A missing child returns from a cult mass with green fog leaking from their mouth.
  • The cult asks Byl to silence a tram bell so it can hear something answering beneath the city.
  • A cult procession moves toward St. Orra’s Colossus during a storm, carrying a relic that should not be alive.
  • The legitimate Church asks Byl and Lott to stop the cult without allowing the Civic Order to massacre the worshippers.
  • The hand points beneath Nine Spoons, where something has begun knocking from below.
